exposure: 2014 ACOG/SMFM Obstetric Care Consensus for Safe Prevention of Primary CD
Implementation of the 2014 ACOG/SMFM Obstetric Care Consensus for Safe Prevention of Primary CD
cohort: 44,001 singleton, cephalic, term pregnancies at a tertiary-care teaching maternity hospital
finding: The 2014 ACOG/SMFM Obstetric Care Consensus for Safe Prevention of Primary CD was not associated with a change in unscheduled CD rates, though VBAC deliveries increased.
mod_finding: The study found that a consensus on safe prevention of primary cesarean delivery did not change unscheduled cesarean delivery rates, but it was associated with an increase in vaginal birth after cesarean (VBAC) deliveries.
